subject: Request: bridging voucher for Skyline Health latency incident
messages:
From: Daniel Wu <daniel.wu@skylinehealth.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, procurement@skylinehealth.com
Date: Tue, 10 Aug 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Production latency spike impacting patient check-ins (incident 2027-08-10)

Vanessa / Redwood team,

We experienced a sustained latency degradation across our API calls this morning between 06:18 and 07:42 PDT. Volume was within normal bounds; error rates remained low but median p95 latency for generation endpoints jumped to ~1.8s from our usual ~220ms. The impact: our patient self-check-in flow timed out for roughly 12% of traffic over a 60-minute window.

This incident caused manual triage at two hospital sites and delayed check-ins for several dozen patients. We need a remediation plan and a discussion about compensation for the operational burden and increased labor costs. Our procurement team will want a concrete proposal we can present to our execs.

Attached: preliminary incident timeline and logs we collected (Fed export). Please let us know what remediation and credit options you can offer.

Thanks,
Daniel
Director, Platform Ops
Skyline Health

[Attachment: incident-timeline-skyline-20270810.pdf (PDF)]

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 10 Aug 2027 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Production latency spike impacting patient check-ins (incident 2027-08-10)

Karthik / Marissa — forwarding Skyline's incident report. Quick context: Skyline is a mid-enterprise customer on a reserved capacity plan with a three-node dedicated pool and a committed monthly spend of ~USD 320k. They hit a brief but high-impact latency window that affected a core patient flow.

Options I recommend for executive signoff (short list):
- Option A (Goodwill voucher): One bridging voucher equal to 100% of their monthly committed capacity (i.e., apply a one-month credit = $320,000) to be applied to the next invoice. Good for retention but high cost.
- Option B (Proportional credit + support): 25% credit of monthly committed spend ($80,000) + 2 weeks of dedicated SRE hours (no charge) + a joint postmortem + SLO amendment (non-admission).
- Option C (Limited credit): Flat one-time $40,000 credit and an offer for a 30% discount on remediation engineering work (invoice separate).

Rationale: the customer is strategic in health vertical; churn risk if not addressed quickly. I'm inclined to propose Option B as our initial ask — balances cost and signal.

Attachments: credit-calculation-sheet.xlsx (breaks down numbers) and a draft SLO amendment for approval.

Can I get an executive clearance to offer Option B? If yes, I will draft a customer-facing note and DocuSign acceptance.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Account Lead, Redwood Inference

[Attachments: credit-calculation-sheet.xlsx (Excel), slo-amendment-draft.docx (DOCX)]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 11 Aug 2027 08:37:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Production latency spike impacting patient check-ins (incident 2027-08-10)

Vanessa — thanks for the quick breakdown. I agree Option B is pragmatic. A few required guardrails before I sign off:

1) Cap the voucher to the lesser of 25% monthly committed spend OR $100k (to avoid open-ended precedent).
2) Credit applied to next invoice only; no retro refunds.
3) Legal to add standard non-admission language and limit downstream liability (we include the SLO amendment language you attached).
4) Include a clause that the customer accepts the DocuSign as full and final settlement for this incident and that recurring SLA adjustments (if any) will be discussed in the renewal cadence.

If Legal and Finance confirm the mechanics, I can approve Option B under the cap above. Please loop Legal (marissa) for a quick read and Procurement contact.

-Karthik
VP, Commercial Operations

- Add-on: two weeks (80 hours) of dedicated SRE support from Redwood (remote), scheduled within 30 days upon request.
- Conditions: Acceptance via DocuSign link confirms settlement for this incident, includes non-admission of liability, and applies to the invoice following acceptance.
- Cap: Per Karthik's ask, this is capped at $100,000 (not applicable here since 25% = $80k).
